hero.title: Ghar ka kharcha,
hero.lead: Log a spend in five seconds, see what is safe to spend today, and run the whole house from one app: splits, shop credit, bills, goals and the shopping list. No account. Nothing leaves your phone.

steps: This is your month.
What you spent, what is left and how far through the budget you are. It opens in a second, with no sign-in.
Four shortcuts, your pick.
Quick access opens the screens you use most. Tap Edit to choose which four sit here.
One number for today.
Safe to spend is what you can still spend today and stay inside the month’s budget. It moves with every entry.
Every spend, one swipe away.
Your latest spends sit under the cards. In Expenses, swipe a row left to delete it, or right to add the same one again.
Say it out loud.
Tap the mic and say “380 frankie by UPI”. The amount, title, category and payment mode fill themselves in.
Your usuals, one tap.
The things you buy again and again wait as chips. Tap one and it is filled in, at the price you last paid.
See where it went.
Categories, the last seven days and who paid, by week, month or year.
One list for the whole house.
Add what the house needs and set how many with − and +. Tick things off in the shop, then log the trip as one expense.
Money lent, papers that expire.
Gharcha reminds you when a loan is due and before a warranty, PUC or insurance runs out.
Save towards something.
Give a goal a target and a month. Gharcha works out what to put aside each month to get there.

day.title: It keeps up without being asked.
day.lead: Five small moments. None of them takes more than a few seconds.
events: One tap on the home-screen widget.
“188 lunch by UPI”, said out loud.
Pasted from the bank message; filed under Petrol.
A doorbell: due in three days.

more.title: Built for how a home really spends.
more.lead: Not just “Food and Transport”: kirana credit, the milk tally, chit funds and the papers in the drawer.

widget: Five to choose from: this month, today, bills, shopping and quick add.
goals: A target, a date and what to put aside each month.
shopping: Tick things off, then log the lot as one expense.
accounts: Cash, bank and wallets, each with a running balance.
budgets: Limits per category and a plain-words forecast.
groups: Home, trips and parties, with who owes whom.
family: A profile, PIN and avatar for every member.
khata: Shop credit, milk and maid tallies, gold and chits.
reminders: Bills that log themselves and nudges that never repeat.
rewards: Ten levels, 33 badges and a shop to spend points in.
avatar: Full outfits, hair and accessories; moods that follow your budget.
sounds: A cooker whistle for nudges, a doorbell for bills.
categories: Add your own, recolour the built-in ones.
data: One-file backup, CSV and PDF export, PIN or fingerprint.
languages: Every screen, badge and notification follows.

trust: Open it and start. Nothing to sign up for.
Everything stays in the phone’s own database.
Back up to one file, export CSV or PDF, erase in one tap.

looks.title: Pick a colour. The whole app follows.
looks.lead: Twenty-four themes in the app; try a few on this page. Then send the family a card in any of five styles.

fest.title: The app dresses up for every festival. So does your avatar.
fest.lead: From three days before to three days after, Home wears the festival’s colours and decor, your avatar gets the outfit, and the first open during the festival plays a celebration.
perks: Themes and decorations switch on 3 days before the festival and stay for 3 days after
A full-screen celebration on first open, with the festival’s own sound and your avatar already dressed up
Tap the festival banner on Home any time to replay the celebration: fireworks, colour clouds, kites, tricolour confetti, petal showers or snow
Claim my gifts: the pack, +50 points and the outfit — free during the window, yours for good
A festival banner on Home with its own looping particle show and a countdown from a week before

steps: Download
Tap Download for Android. The APK is the build this page was published with, so it is always the latest one that passed.
Allow the install
Open the file; Android asks once to allow installs from your browser or file manager. Later builds install over it and keep your data.
Set up
Pick a language, your name and mobile, a currency and an optional budget. A daily 8:30 PM nudge is ready for you; App lock is a switch on Me whenever you want it.
Moving from HomeQuest?
Gharcha is a new app with its own id. Export a CSV from HomeQuest (Me → Your data) and import it in Gharcha (Me → Your data → Import CSV).
